summary: Prompt 4 assignment feature backend testing: 32/32 new tests pass (client created_by stamping + migration, assignment CRUD + validations, /assignments/check permission matrix, edit-barcode/undo-edit/reco-adjustments ACL gates, revoke + post-revoke removal, cycle-count day/project owner gates). REGRESSION DETECTED in prompt 1-2-3 tests (16 failed): legacy tests pass `user_id` in body / X-User-Id header as audit-trail attribution for a non-owner user, but new ACL gate now treats that as the actor and returns 403.

critical.issue: ACL gate reads actor from body `adj.user_id` / `data.get('user_id')` as a fallback to the X-User-Id header. Existing prompt 1/2 audit-log tests send a non-owner user_id for audit-trail attribution only, which now incorrectly triggers the assignment ACL check and returns 403. Spec says: 'missing X-User-Id header is treated as legacy/no-check', but the code's fallback to body user_id breaks that contract.

Same root cause via X-User-Id header. Existing prompt 1 test_audit_movement_log.py sends X-User-Id = TEST_USER_ID (a non-owner created for audit-trail) and now gets 403 from _require_owner_for_session. Either tests need to use the owner's id, or the gate should accept the request when the X-User-Id user is unknown/legacy.

action_items: Decide actor-vs-audit-trail semantics for X-User-Id and adj.user_id. Recommended: For ACL only read the X-User-Id header (NOT body user_id), and either (a) update legacy tests to send the client owner's user_id, or (b) introduce a separate `X-Actor-Id` header so audit-trail user_id doesn't conflict with ACL principal.

Patch /reports/edit-barcode (line ~3096), /reports/undo-edit (line ~3350), /reco-adjustments (line ~3814) — remove the `or adj.user_id` / `or data.get('user_id')` fallback in actor_id resolution so that body-supplied user_id is used ONLY for audit-trail logging, not ACL gating.
After patch, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_audit_movement_log.py and test_last_edited_popup_backend.py to confirm regressions resolved.
Consider adding an integration test that asserts: when X-User-Id is absent but body carries user_id, no 403 is raised (legacy behaviour).
critical_code_review_comments: audit_routes.py is 7328 lines — well past the 700-line guidance. Split into routers (clients, sessions, reports, reco, assignments, users).

assignment_helper.create_assignment does NOT check for duplicate active assignments — the same (assigned_to, session_id) can be inserted multiple times. Consider an upsert or a uniqueness guard so /by-me doesn't show duplicates and /check doesn't iterate dead rows.

check_assignment_access returns can_edit_reco=True when report_type is omitted (`(not rt_norm and True)`). This is permissive for callers that forget to pass report_type — recommend defaulting to False unless explicit.

DELETE /assignments/{id} is idempotent for already-revoked rows, but it bypasses the ownership check (returns success without verifying assigned_by) — minor info-disclosure: a 3rd party could detect that an assignment_id exists. Move the assigned_by check before the is_active short-circuit.

create_client falls back to admin's id when X-User-Id is empty — fine for migration, but in steady-state this attributes anonymous create operations to admin which can hide intent. Consider rejecting with 401 when X-User-Id is missing on /clients POST, once the FE consistently sends it.
/assignments/users response is not paginated (to_list(2000)). Fine today, but should bound for large portals.

success_rate.backend: 100% on Prompt-4 assignment tests (32/32); regression suite drops to ~73% (43/59 + 7 errors) due to the actor-fallback bug described above

test_credentials: Admin username=admin password=admin123 (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md). Tests dynamically register TEST_assignee_* and TEST_stranger_* users via /register then approve via admin /users/{id}/approve.
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_-prefixed clients, sessions, portal users, and one transient barcode_edits row (deleted in finally). Cycle-count tests create a TEST_cc_ client + project + day.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All prompt-4 assertions are green. The remaining work is: (1) main agent fixes the actor-fallback so adj.user_id in body is not used for ACL; (2) re-run /app/backend/tests/test_assignment_feature.py to confirm no prompt-4 regression and /app/backend/tests/test_audit_movement_log.py + test_last_edited_popup_backend.py for regression closure. The portal route prefix is /api/audit/portal (not /api directly) — easy to miss. Cycle-count router prefix is /api/audit/portal/cycle-count.
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: actor_id in reco-adjustments / edit-barcode / undo-edit is resolved as `(X-User-Id header) or (body user_id) or ''`. Legacy callers (prompt 1/2/3 tests) pass body user_id PURELY for audit-trail attribution (so the Movement Log knows who saved the row). Prompt 4's gate now interprets that same field as the auth principal and 403's any non-owner. Reproduction: POST /api/audit/portal/reco-adjustments with no X-User-Id header but body {"user_id":"some-random-id", "client_id":"..."} → 403 instead of 200. Mitigation: read actor strictly from `X-User-Id` header (or a dedicated `X-Actor-Id`), and keep body user_id solely for audit-trail. Same pattern applies to /reports/edit-barcode and /reports/undo-edit.
